title: Smt. Shakuntla Devi v. State of U.P. — bill dispute relegated to Clause 5.6
coram: Arun Tandon, J.; Shashi Kant, J.
disposition: Writ dismissed; consumer relegated to Clause 5.6.
headnote: A Division Bench of the Allahabad High Court dismissed a writ petition challenging an electricity consumption bill, holding that a consumer dissatisfied with such a bill has a remedy under Clause 5.6 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, and granting liberty to pursue that remedy.
facts: Smt. Shakuntla Devi filed a writ petition in the Allahabad High Court against the State of Uttar Pradesh and two others, including the electricity corporation, challenging a bill raised for her electricity consumption. Counsel for the petitioner was Rahul Malviya; Sri R.S. Umrao appeared for respondents 2 and 3. The order does not record the bill amount, the period, or whether the dispute concerned a defective meter or ordinary billing.

holding_units.holding: A consumer dissatisfied with a bill raised for electricity consumption has a remedy under Clause 5.6 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005; a writ petition challenging such a bill is dismissed with liberty to pursue that remedy.

not_decided.note: Merits of the bill left to the Clause 5.6 remedy.
